news.title: European spacecraft finds chaotic scene after asteroid deflection experiment
paras: Hello again European spacecraft finds chaotic scene after asteroid deflection experiment “DART made a really, really large mess. However, we didn’t really know what kind of mess.”

This image from the Hera spacecraft's asteroid framing camera shows Didymos and its smaller companion Dimorphos, revealing the stadium-sized crater created by the impact of NASA's DART spacecraft in 2022. The first-of-its-kind experiment worked beautifully as the solar-powered space probe slammed into asteroid Dimorphos, permanently altering its trajectory. Using telescopes, astronomers measured changes in the orbit of Dimorphos around a larger asteroid companion named Didymos in the aftermath of NASA’s Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission.

sport.title: How the ATP top 10 rankings at the end of 2026 compared to those from 2016
paras: Carlos Alcaraz secured his sixth ATP title of the year after defeating Alexander Zverev in Sunday’s ATP Finals final. The victory did little to shake up the ATP rankings – Alcaraz remains in the number three spot, behind Alexander Zverev and Jannik Sinner.

Zverev ended the season as world number one for the first time in his career, thanks in large part to the injuries suffered by Alcaraz and Sinner throughout 2026. Sinner is set to slide down the rankings in 2027, as he will be recovering from knee surgery for an extended period.

sport.title: Data proves why Aryna Sabalenka should not be underestimated heading into 2027
paras: The nail in the coffin of Aryna Sabalenka’s 2026 WTA campaign was administered earlier this month. Sabalenka , the former world number one, failed to advance out of her WTA Finals group for the first time since 2021, losing to Mirra Andreeva and Elina Svitolina .

The Belarusian has struggled on the Tour since winning the coveted ‘Sunshine Double’ , suffering damaging losses to a number of lower-ranked players. Sabalenka’s woes came to a head in Indian Wells – Andreeva’s title-winning campaign in California saw Sabalenka slip to world number three for the first time since August 2024.

sport.title: Why the first tournament of Alex de Minaur’s 2027 season could define his Australian Open campaign
paras: The Australian star failed to leave a significant impression on the 2026 season, losing before the quarter-finals at three of the four Grand Slams and reaching the last eight at just two of the nine Masters 1000 events. De Minaur began the year ranked sixth in the ATP rankings.

He has since fallen five places to world number 11. However, De Minaur’s campaign has not been a complete disaster – it would be unfair to label it as such. He won the Rotterdam Open title for the first time and qualified for finals in ‘s-Hertogenbosch, Beijing and Vienna.

sport.title: November 26, 1998: The day Pete Sampras secured the year-end No 1 ranking for a record sixth straight time
paras: Every day, Tennis Majors takes you back to a big moment in tennis history. On November 26, 1998, Pete Sampras set a new record by logging his sixth consecutive year-end No 1 ranking after playing a gruelling schedule post the US Open

On this day, November 26, 1998, Pete Sampras secured the year-end world No 1ranking for an unprecedented sixth consecutive time. Ironically, the news came when world No 2 Marcelo Rios pulled out during the ATP Tour World Championships, an announcement that was made on Pete’s day off. Pete Sampras, born in 1971, dominated the game in the 1990s.

sport.title: Comparing Mirra Andreeva’s 2026 season to what Serena Williams did at the same age
paras: Mirra Andreeva won her first Grand Slam title in 2026 and finished the year second in the world. Andreeva turned 19 this year, and became one of the best players in women’s tennis. She will begin the 2027 season within touching distance of Elena Rybakina, the world number one.

Making a significant step forward at such a young age, it’s no surprise that Andreeva has been compared to the likes of Serena Williams . But how do they compare at the same age? Andreeva turned 19 in April 2026 and won her maiden Grand Slam title shortly after at Roland Garros.
